title: Commons application modules do not import integration

facts.note: File path places the module in a commons/shared application tree.
Layer segment derived from path; files with no layer segment are out of scope.

Import-resolution observer needed to know that any import in the module (newly added or already present) resolves into the commons integration/ layer; bare npm specifiers are not resolved into the project graph.

fires: A module under commons/application/ has a relative or project-alias import (added or pre-existing) that resolves into the commons integration/ layer.
A module under shared/application/ imports a transport client or adapter from integration/ to make an acceptance pass quickly.
doesNotFire: A test file under commons/application/ imports from integration/ (test files are never scanned).
A file in a vendored or build directory imports from integration/.
A commons application module imports a bare npm specifier (resolved outside the project graph).
A file whose path carries no layer segment imports from integration/.
A commons application module imports an application-facing port it defines.

given: A module under `commons/application/` or `shared/application/` (orchestration over ports it defines)
when: it adds or keeps an import resolving into the commons `integration/` layer
then: The module MUST NOT import from the commons `integration/` layer.
prefer: Canonical path: keep commons application code dependent on an application-facing port.
Canonical path: let integration implement that port and the composition root supply it.
During GREEN: first reuse an existing port that already represents the required capability.
During GREEN: add the smallest missing port only when current behavior genuinely needs an outer capability.
During GREEN: pass only the data or collaborator required by the acceptance.
avoid: Importing integration directly as a shortcut to GREEN.
Introducing a generalized service layer for future callers.
unless: Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
Bare npm specifiers resolve outside the project graph; not layer-checked.
A file with no layer segment is outside these rules, not in violation.
why: Application orchestrates through ports it defines; reaching into integration inverts the dependency and welds orchestration to a transport, so changing the transport changes the orchestration.
evidence: Commons application has no integration dependency: bun_clean_architecture_detector reports no import from a commons/shared application module resolving into the integration layer.
verifier_detail: Flag an import from a commons application module (path under `commons/application/` or `shared/application/`) that resolves into the commons `integration/` layer.
Skip test files and vendored/build directories entirely.
Do not layer-check bare npm specifiers; they resolve outside the project graph.
Files with no layer segment are out of scope, not violations.

sharedNodes.text: Prove: the current behavioral acceptance passes. Do not broaden: do not reorganize unrelated modules.
